deal_breakers.title: Asymmetric Termination Rights
deal_breakers.claim: The Provider has the right to terminate for convenience with 15 days' notice, while the Customer can only terminate for convenience after 12 months with 60 days' notice.
deal_breakers.plain_english: The Provider can walk away from the contract at any time with only 15 days' notice, giving your business very little time to find an alternative vendor or migrate your data.
deal_breakers.why_flagged:
1. Provider has a unilateral convenience termination right.
2. 15-day notice period is unusually short for enterprise software services.
3. Customer's convenience termination right is locked for 12 months with a 60-day notice.
deal_breakers.suggested_negotiation: Customer proposes modifying Section 10.3 to require at least 60 days' written notice for convenience termination, and granting Customer reciprocal convenience termination rights with the same notice.

missing_clauses.title: Disaster Recovery SLA & RTO/RPO
missing_clauses.why_it_matters: The contract does not define explicit Recovery Time Objectives (RTO) or Recovery Point Objectives (RPO). If Provider suffers a catastrophic datacenter outage, there is no contractual commitment for when service or data will be restored.
missing_clauses.recommended_clause: Provider shall maintain a business continuity and disaster recovery plan with a Recovery Time Objective (RTO) of not more than 4 hours and a Recovery Point Objective (RPO) of not more than 1 hour.
missing_clauses.evidence_snippet: No disaster recovery SLA or RTO/RPO targets found.

missing_clauses.title: Maximum Security Incident Notification Window
missing_clauses.why_it_matters: Section 4.3 only requires notice 'without undue delay'. It lacks an explicit hour-based maximum window (e.g., within 24 to 72 hours). Without a strict timeframe, Customer may fail to meet mandatory regulatory reporting deadlines.
missing_clauses.recommended_clause: Provider shall notify Customer in writing without undue delay, and in any event within forty-eight (48) hours, after becoming aware of or confirming any Security Incident involving Customer Data.
missing_clauses.evidence_snippet: Section 4.3 specifies 'without undue delay', but omits an explicit hour-based SLA.

missing_clauses.title: Affirmative Data Deletion & Certification
missing_clauses.why_it_matters: The agreement permits Provider to retain backups for up to 180 days, but lacks an affirmative obligation for Provider to return all Customer Data upon expiration and certify permanent destruction in writing.
missing_clauses.recommended_clause: Within thirty (30) days of termination, Provider shall, at Customer's election, return or permanently and securely destroy all Customer Data, and deliver written certification of compliance signed by an officer of Provider.
missing_clauses.evidence_snippet: Permits 180-day backup retention, but lacks affirmative destruction certification.

missing_clauses.title: Advance Notice of New Subprocessors
missing_clauses.why_it_matters: Section 4.2 allows Provider to use subcontractors without prior notification or opportunity for Customer to object, which may violate Customer compliance standards or data residency policies.
missing_clauses.recommended_clause: Provider shall provide Customer with at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice before engaging any new subcontractor to process Customer Data, and Customer may object on reasonable security or compliance grounds.
missing_clauses.evidence_snippet: Section 4.2 permits subcontractors without advance notice or objection rights.

missing_clauses.title: Termination Right for Extended Force Majeure
missing_clauses.why_it_matters: Section 15 suspends liability during Force Majeure events, but gives Customer no right to terminate the contract if the outage or failure lasts for an extended period (e.g., longer than 30 consecutive days).
missing_clauses.recommended_clause: If a Force Majeure event prevents performance of the Services for more than thirty (30) consecutive days, Customer may terminate this Agreement immediately upon written notice without penalty.
missing_clauses.evidence_snippet: Section 15 suspends performance but provides no exit right for extended outages.

missing_clauses.title: Customer Convenience Termination Parity
missing_clauses.why_it_matters: Provider can terminate for convenience at any time upon 15 days' notice, but Customer is barred from terminating during the first 12 months and must provide 60 days' notice thereafter.
missing_clauses.recommended_clause: Either Party may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time upon sixty (60) days' prior written notice.
missing_clauses.evidence_snippet: Section 10.4 locks Customer for 12 months with 60-day notice, while Section 10.3 allows Provider 15-day exit.

missing_clauses.title: Cyber Liability & E&O Insurance Commitments
missing_clauses.why_it_matters: The agreement contains no requirement for Provider to maintain Technology Errors & Omissions or Cyber Liability insurance to backstop its indemnification and security commitments.
missing_clauses.recommended_clause: Provider shall maintain commercial general liability insurance, technology errors & omissions, and cyber liability insurance with policy limits of not less than $5,000,000 per occurrence during the Term.

risks.observation: Standard tier charges ₹12 per document overage, which is 140% higher than the Enterprise overage rate (₹5/doc). Unanticipated processing spikes could result in unpredictable monthly invoice surges.
risks.recommendation: Negotiate a monthly overage cap (e.g., maximum 20% over base fee) or an automatic tier bump mechanism when usage consistently exceeds included quota.

risks.risk_title: Absence of Price Protection / Cap on Renewal
risks.observation: The pricing table does not define annual fee adjustment limits (e.g. CPI or maximum 3-5% increase). Upon automatic renewal, Provider is not contractually restricted from raising monthly tier fees.
risks.recommendation: Insert a price escalation cap: 'Fees shall not increase by more than 3% annually upon renewal.'

MASTER SOFTWARE SERVICES AND DATA
PROCESSING AGREEMENT
Agreement Date: 15 September 2026    Agreement ID: MSA-2026-0915-47
This Master Software Services and Data Processing Agreement (the “Agreement”) is entered into by and between
Northstar Analytics Pvt. Ltd., a company incorporated under the laws of India, with its principal office at
Bengaluru, Karnataka (“Customer”), and Meridian Cloud Systems Pvt. Ltd., a company incorporated under the
laws of India, with its principal office at Hyderabad, Telangana (“Provider”). Customer and Provider are each a
“Party” and together the “Parties.”
1. DEFINITIONS
1.1 Confidential Information means non-public business, technical, financial, customer, security, product, pricing,
and operational information disclosed by either Party, whether marked confidential or whether a reasonable person
would understand the information to be confidential.
1.2 Customer Data means all information submitted to the Services by Customer or on Customer’s behalf,
including personal information, documents, source material, usage information, and audit records.
1.3 Services means the hosted analytics, document processing, reporting, API access, and related support
services described in this Agreement and its Schedules.
2. SERVICES AND SERVICE LEVELS
2.1 Provider shall provide the Services substantially in accordance with Schedule A. Provider may modify
non-material features from time to time, provided that such modification does not materially reduce the core
functionality of the Services.
2.2 Provider will use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain 99.5% monthly availability, excluding scheduled
maintenance, emergency maintenance, force majeure events, failures caused by Customer, and third-party
services outside Provider’s reasonable control.
2.3 Scheduled maintenance will normally be communicated at least 24 hours in advance. Emergency maintenance
may occur without prior notice where Provider reasonably believes that delay would create a security or
operational risk.
3. FEES AND PAYMENT

3.1 Invoices are payable within 30 days of receipt. Undisputed late amounts may accrue interest at 1.5% per
month or the maximum rate permitted by applicable law, whichever is lower.
3.2 Provider may suspend access for invoices more than 15 days overdue after providing Customer with at least 7
days’ written notice and an opportunity to cure.
4. DATA PROCESSING AND SECURITY
4.1 Provider shall process Customer Data only to provide, secure, maintain, and improve the Services and to
comply with applicable law. Provider shall implement reasonable administrative, technical, and physical safeguards

appropriate to the nature of the data processed.
4.2 Provider may use subcontractors to process Customer Data. Provider remains responsible for the acts and
omissions of its subcontractors to the same extent as if those acts or omissions were performed by Provider.
4.3 Provider shall notify Customer without undue delay after confirming a Security Incident involving unauthorized
access to Customer Data and shall provide reasonably available information concerning the nature and scope of
the incident.
4.4 Provider may retain backup copies of Customer Data for up to 180 days after deletion from production
systems, provided such copies remain protected and are not restored except for disaster recovery purposes.
5. CONFIDENTIALITY
5.1 Each Party shall protect the other Party’s Confidential Information using at least reasonable care and shall use
such information only to perform or receive rights under this Agreement.
5.2 The confidentiality obligations do not apply to information that the receiving Party can demonstrate was already
lawfully known, becomes public without breach, is independently developed, or is lawfully received from a third
party without a duty of confidentiality.
5.3 If disclosure is required by law, the receiving Party shall, where legally permitted, provide prompt notice and
reasonable cooperation so the disclosing Party may seek protective relief.
6. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY
6.1 Customer retains all right, title, and interest in Customer Data. Provider retains all right, title, and interest in the
Services, software, models, templates, documentation, and Provider-developed technology.
6.2 Subject to payment of all applicable fees, Provider grants Customer a non-exclusive, non-transferable,
worldwide license during the Term to use the Services for Customer’s internal business operations.
6.3 Feedback provided by Customer may be used by Provider to improve its products and services, provided
Provider does not disclose Customer Confidential Information in doing so.

7. WARRANTIES
7.1 Each Party represents that it has authority to enter into this Agreement. Provider warrants that the Services will
materially conform to the applicable documentation during the Term.
7.2 Except as expressly stated in this Agreement, the Services are provided on an “as available” basis and
Provider disclaims all other warranties to the maximum extent permitted by law.
8. INDEMNIFICATION
8.1 Provider shall defend Customer against a third-party claim alleging that the Services, when used as permitted
by this Agreement, infringe a third party’s registered intellectual property right, and shall pay damages finally
awarded or settlements approved by Provider.
8.2 Customer shall defend Provider against third-party claims arising from Customer Data or Customer’s unlawful
use of the Services, and shall pay damages finally awarded or settlements approved by Customer.
8.3 The indemnified Party shall promptly notify the indemnifying Party of a claim and provide reasonable
cooperation. The indemnifying Party shall control the defense, provided it may not settle a claim in a manner that
admits liability or imposes non-monetary obligations on the indemnified Party without consent.
9. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY
9.1 TO THE MAXIMUM EXTENT PERMITTED BY LAW, NEITHER PARTY SHALL BE LIABLE FOR INDIRECT,
INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, EXEMPLARY, OR PUNITIVE DAMAGES, OR FOR LOST
PROFITS, REVENUE, OR DATA.
9.2 EXCEPT FOR CUSTOMER’S PAYMENT OBLIGATIONS, EACH PARTY’S AGGREGATE LIABILITY ARISING
OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT EXCEED THE FEES PAID OR PAYABLE BY
CUSTOMER TO PROVIDER DURING THE THREE MONTHS PRECEDING THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE
CLAIM.
9.3 The limitations in Sections 9.1 and 9.2 shall not apply to fraud, willful misconduct, or a Party’s indemnification
obligations under Section 8.
10. TERMINATION
10.1 Either Party may terminate this Agreement for material breach if the breach remains uncured for 30 days after
written notice describing the breach.
10.2 Either Party may terminate immediately upon written notice if the other Party becomes insolvent, enters
liquidation, or ceases substantially all business operations.
10.3 Provider may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time upon 15 days’ written notice to Customer.
10.4 Customer may terminate for convenience only after the first 12 months of the Term and upon 60 days’ written
notice.
11. NON-SOLICITATION
11.1 During the Term and for 24 months thereafter, Customer shall not directly or indirectly solicit for employment
any employee of Provider who materially participated in delivering the Services. This restriction shall not apply to
general advertisements not specifically targeted at Provider employees.
12. GOVERNING LAW AND DISPUTES
12.1 This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of India, without regard to conflict-of-law principles.
12.2 The Parties shall first attempt in good faith to resolve disputes through executive-level negotiation. If a dispute
is not resolved within 30 days, it shall be finally resolved by arbitration in Bengaluru, India, by a sole arbitrator

appointed in accordance with applicable arbitration law.
13. NOTICES
Notices under this Agreement must be in writing and delivered by courier, registered post, or email to the
addresses specified below. Email notices are effective upon confirmation of transmission, provided no delivery
failure notice is received.

14. TERM AND RENEWAL
14.1 The initial Term begins on the Agreement Date and continues for 24 months.
14.2 Unless either Party gives written notice of non-renewal at least 90 days before expiration, the Agreement will
automatically renew for successive 12-month periods.
15. FORCE MAJEURE
Neither Party shall be liable for delay or failure to perform caused by events beyond its reasonable control,
including natural disasters, war, terrorism, government action, widespread internet failures, or labor disruptions,
provided that the affected Party uses reasonable efforts to mitigate the effects.
16. ASSIGNMENT
Neither Party may assign this Agreement without the other Party’s prior written consent, except that either Party
may assign the Agreement without consent to an affiliate or in connection with a merger, acquisition, corporate
reorganization, or sale of substantially all assets, provided the assignee assumes the assigning Party’s obligations.
17. ORDER OF PRECEDENCE
If there is a conflict between this Agreement and a Schedule, the following order of precedence applies: (1) the
applicable Data Processing Addendum, (2) the applicable Order Form, (3) this Agreement, and (4) all other
Schedules, unless the conflicting document expressly identifies the provision of this Agreement that it overrides.
18. AUDIT RIGHTS
Customer may, no more than once per calendar year and upon 20 business days’ prior written notice, audit
Provider’s compliance with the security obligations in Section 4. Provider may satisfy the request by providing an
independent third-party security report where reasonably sufficient to address the requested controls.
19. PUBLICITY
